title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-04-20
content:
Week of 2026-04-20: Infrastructure Weekly Update - GPU fleet, Regions, Capacity planning

Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Marcus Li, Sofia Martinez, Daniel Kim, Olivia Baker (SRE sync)

Executive summary:
- Overall GPU utilization for serving clusters averaged 74% this week (up from 68% last week).
- Spot shortages observed in us-west-2 (SFO) during peak evening window; several allocation fallbacks to us-east-1 (EWR) occurred.
- Short-term capacity gap estimated: need +120 A100-equivalent GPUs across US regions to maintain 95th pct latency SLO for long-context workloads.
- Cost optimization pilot (multi-queue scheduling + aggressive prefix cache) projected to reduce token cost by ~9% if rolled out next quarter.

Metrics snapshot (week-over-week):
- Avg GPU util: 74% (prev 68%)
- 95th percentile token latency: 220ms (prev 200ms)
- Long-seq job tail 99th pctl latency: 1.6s (prev 1.2s)
- Preemptions (spot pools): 18 incidents (down from 24)
- Failed containers due to OOM on quantized models: 3 (investigating model memory accounting)

Regions update:
- us-west-2 (SFO): observed capacity pressure between 18:00-23:00 PDT. Autoscaler triggered burst to dedicated reserve twice; saw fallbacks to us-east-1 for 14% of requests during spikes.
- us-east-1 (EWR): nominal, has headroom but higher cost per-token for some instance types.
- eu-west-1: stable; beginning pilot on new NCCL tuning for multi-GPU batching.
- ap-southeast-1: planning phase for Q3 private deployments; no immediate capacity changes.

GPU fleet and procurement:
- Procurement update: vendor confirmed shipment ETA for 240 A100-80GB equivalents with staggered delivery starting 2026-06-10. Procurement team requested confirmation to convert 40 of those to L40s for research; we recommended 20 L40 / 220 A100 mix to prioritize serving throughput.
- Short-term plan: reallocate 60 GPUs from internal training pool to serving reserve for May; will be temporary and tracked via INFRA-842.

Capacity planning and forecasts:
- Forecast model (traffic growth + new customers): 18% Q over Q growth in inference tokens. Under conservative scenario, we need +350 GPUs by end of Q3; under optimistic reuse/caching and quantization rollout, gap reduces to +210 GPUs.
- Planned mitigations: 1) aggressive prefix/KV cache rollout (optimize feature) 2) prioritized quantization profiles for 30% of model traffic 3) regional routing to favor regions with spare capacity during peaks.

Operational incidents this week:
- 2026-04-18 19:42 PDT: Regional capacity fallback in us-west-2 affecting 3 customers; root cause: unexpected spot reclamation combined with conservative autoscaler thresholds. Resolution: lowered autoscaler threshold and enabled burst to dedicated reserve earlier. Action: refine autoscaler policy (see action items).
- 2026-04-19 11:05 UTC: One deploy caused KV cache cold-start regressions for chat flows; mitigated by staged rollout and cache warmup script.

Decisions made:
- Approve temporary reallocation of 60 GPUs from training to serving for May (Aisha / Marcus approved).
- Proceed with procurement mix recommendation: 20 L40 + 220 A100 (pending finance sign-off).
- Start canary of multi-queue scheduler in us-west-2 next week (limit to 10% of traffic).

Risks & open questions:
- If vendor shipment slips beyond July, Q3 capacity gap will widen and impact onboarding timelines for two mid-market customers. Contingency: convertible contracts with cloud partners to burst on-demand at higher cost.
- Potential performance regressions from quantized model variants on long-context workloads; need dedicated evals and guardrails.

Action items (owner - due):
- Refine autoscaler policy to reduce fallback rate (Marcus Li - 2026-04-27)
- Implement cache warmup and monitor for 2 weeks (Sofia Martinez - 2026-05-04)
- Update capacity forecast with procurement shipping schedule and new Q growth model (Daniel Kim - 2026-04-24)
- Kick off canary of multi-queue scheduler in us-west-2 (Aisha Patel / Release eng - 2026-04-28)
- Add regression tests for quantized long-context workloads to CI (Applied ML - 2026-05-03)

Notes / quick wins:
- Short-term QoS tweak: deprioritize background batch requests during 18:00-23:00 PDT to free serving headroom. Engineering agrees to a 2-week trial.
- Cost idea: enable mixed-instance scheduling for low-priority workloads to reduce preemption impact.

Appendix: links and references:
- INFRA-842: reallocation request and tracking ticket (linked above).
- Confluence planning page for Q3 capacity and procurement (linked above).
- PR with autoscaler threshold change: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/416

Next meeting: 2026-04-27 weekly sync, 10:00 PDT
